# FDG3058

> DO add the suffix “Collection,” except for reusable, specialized data types such as “Queue” and “HashSet.”

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 3.5.2 Names of Common Types. Applies to: IEnumerable ICollection IList IEnumerable&lt;T> ICollection&lt;T> IList&lt;T>.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1710
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

CA1710 does not know the exception for reusable, specialized data structures, so coverage is partial; a report on such a type is not a violation and can be suppressed. Because the package sets dotnet_code_quality.CA1710.exclude_indirect_base_types = false (see FDG3048), CA1710 also reports a type derived from List&lt;T>, Collection&lt;T> or ObservableCollection&lt;T> and a type that implements only IEnumerable&lt;T> (probe with SDK 10.0.403). On the noise samples the option added 2 reports, both classes derived from ObservableCollection&lt;T> that hold a list of items and end in List; both are true warnings (docs/noise-samples.md). Renaming a public type changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; CA1710 has no code fix.
